0.title: Form Shooting Progression
0.cue: Maintain rhythmic rhythm from 5 feet; focus on consistent high release and soft touch.
0.description: Step 5 feet from the rim. Focus on fluid kinetic transfer from ankles to fingertips.

1.title: One-Handed Wall Touches
1.cue: Keep your shooting elbow tucked above eyebrow level before initiating upward thrust.
1.description: Stand 6 inches from a gym wall. Elevate your shooting arm so the ball brushes the wall without your elbow flaring outward or dropping.

2.title: Gooey Wrist-Snap Holds
2.cue: Hold your 'goose neck' follow-through until the basketball touches the hardwood.
2.description: Shoot stationary form shots into the air or basket. Keep the shooting wrist fully flexed downward with fingers pointed towards the floor for 2 full seconds.

3.title: Line Jump Shooting
3.cue: Land with balanced shoulder-width feet exactly on the painted sideline without swaying.
3.description: Align your shooting foot along the sideline. Jump vertically, release, and land smoothly in the identical footprint with zero lateral lean.

4.title: Chair Dip Rhythm Shooting
4.cue: Allow your legs to reach 90% full extension before unlocking your elbow and wrist.
4.description: Begin with hips loaded over a chair. Rise upward into full triple extension before initiating the arm lift, coordinating momentum transfer.

consequence_explanations.0: Your kinetic chain demonstrates optimal sequential power transfer and release trajectory. Maintain this muscle memory.
consequence_explanations.1: Pushing the ball outward rather than elevating upward flattens your launch angle, increasing sensitivity to release velocity errors and causing front-rim misses.
consequence_explanations.2: Truncating wrist extension immediately after release eliminates aerodynamic backspin, producing inconsistent ball flight and unpredictable bounces off the rim.
consequence_explanations.3: Excessive trunk tilt and lateral sway disrupt the vertical kinetic chain, leaking momentum and introducing rotational torque that pushes shots left or right.
consequence_explanations.4: Releasing the ball before lower-body leg drive peaks forces the shoulder and arm muscles to overcompensate, degrading touch and shooting distance consistency.
